content.thinking:
I'm planning the elf archer's full skeleton structure carefully, working out hips, spine, neck, head, arms and legs using model-space coordinates to avoid risky local-axis API calls before writing anything.

Simplifying to a neck chain of two spans plus a head joint angled forward, with head center around y=1.77 giving a believable elf proportion with room for ears and hair. Then I add a jaw joint under the head for small mouth movement, and start planning shoulder placement at x=±0.2, y=1.42 for an A-pose archer stance with arms angled outward.

Now I'm computing elbow and wrist positions for the A-pose to check arm segment lengths stay realistic, placing the bow vertically in the left hand near the wrist with the grip roughly centered on the body height, and mirroring the right arm to hold loosely at the hip, leaving the right hand open to later hold an arrow.

Defining the arm joint chains...

Writing arm sweep code...

I'm also weighing how cel-shaded flat paints will affect texture atlas density, since the model has a lot of surface area to cover at a reasonable texel resolution.

I'll set up a helper for cel-shaded colors, using it consistently across most parts for visual coherence, reserving flat colors only for tiny negligible details like gold trims. Now I'm thinking through how to loft the torso along the spine using bone-chain stations.

For the torso I'm thinking green cel-shaded tunic, then adding a belt by extracting a loop from the surface at a fixed height and sweeping a thin tube around it with carried weights. Now I'm starting to work out the hips and skirt shape of the tunic.

For the lower garment, I'm skipping the lathe approach and instead planning a tabard-style panel hanging in front and back, extruded from a flat outline positioned at the belt line so it drapes between the thighs without clipping the torso or legs. I'm sketching the outline points for that tabard shape now.

For the surface detail, I'll add a simple gold embroidered center stripe on the tabard using a paint function keyed to distance from the midline rather than attempting a full diamond pattern, since that's getting too complex for now.

I'm thinking through a flowing cape on the back, positioned behind the shoulders and flaring wider toward the bottom, colored deep green with a lighter lining and gold trim, while keeping it clear of the arms and layered behind the quiver. I also want to add a bunched hood collar at the neck using a torus-like sweep shape.

Now I'm sketching leaf-shaped pauldrons on the shoulders in gold and leather, and moving on to the legs, setting hip joints and thigh/shin limb lengths to position the feet near the ankles.

I'll add the toe joint parented to the leg chain's tip, then design tall elf-style boots by sweeping the leg with a color and radius gradient — leggings on the thigh transitioning to boot leather lower on the shin, with radius tapering from thigh to knee to calf to ankle.

Still working out boot cuff placement...

Now for the foot, I'll make the toe pointed using a capsule sweep from ankle down to toe tip, tapering the radius for a boot-like shape.

Now I'm working out the arms and hands—building palm boxes and capsule tubes from wrist to fingertip, then adding curled fingers for the left gripping hand versus relaxed open fingers for the right, computing directions from the forearm vectors to position each segment.

Simplifying to a fist ellipsoid for the hand with four finger capsules wrapping over the front of the grip rod, positioned at stacked heights to simulate curling around the bow.

I'm working out the bow's orientation in space — it sits in the vertical YZ plane at x=0.5, with the grip at center and limbs curving so the string faces the archer's body (toward −z) while the tips curve forward, matching how a recurve bow looks when held at rest before drawing.

Working out the bow curve coordinates, aiming for roughly a 1.2m tall elvish longbow gripped near the hand at y≈0.97, with the tips curving back toward the archer and the belly bulging slightly toward the target.

Adding bow details with gold nocks, a wrapped leather grip, and decorative color bands along the limbs.

Now I'm shaping the head: a scaled skull sphere for the cranium positioned near the top, with a separate smaller wedge-shaped sphere for the jaw placed lower and slightly forward to define the chin and face proportions for an elegant elf-like look.

I'm figuring out eye placement by projecting onto the skull's curved surface near the front, setting the eye height around the mid-point of the head and spacing the pair roughly 0.08 apart, checking that the sizes fit within the skull's width at that depth.

For facial details, I'm planning a small cone for the nose, a thin curved sweep in dark red for the mouth, and blush within the eye texture, while working out the chin and jaw positions relative to where the skull sphere's bottom edge sits.

Still placing jaw geometry...

I'm positioning the nose spike based on the skull curvature at that height, then working out the elf ear shape—extruded leaf-like outlines swept back and upward from the sides of the head.

Still working out ear orientation vectors...

Adjusting ear outline points...

Now thinking about hair: silver/white-blonde for the ranger elf look, styled as a cap sphere layered over the skull, offset back and up.

For the back hair, I'm planning a braided chain sweeping from the nape down the back with a few control points, tapered with gold ties at the ends, parented to the head joint rather than a full joint chain for simplicity.

I realize a full sphere for the hair cap would cover the face, so I need a partial sphere using limited theta/phi ranges to form just the top and back coverage, then tilt it backward with a rotation around the X axis to keep the forehead exposed.

Working through the geometry, since the pole axis tilts back 28°, the angle between the axis and the front direction becomes about 118°, while the cap only extends to 112° from the pole — meaning the front rim sits roughly 6° above the horizontal, near the eyebrow line.

I want the hairline closer to the forehead at about 35° elevation, giving a rim angle of 83° (1.45 rad), which naturally covers the back down to around -21° at the nape, and at the sides leaves the hair ending just above ear level near the temple — a believable hairline shape overall.

Now I need sideburns to fill in that gap, extending the rim angle to about 89° (1.55 rad). For the bangs and ponytail, I'm sketching out several tapering strand sweeps curving from the front hairline down over the forehead, calculating how far each spike should hang based on the skull's curvature at that height.

Modeling swoop locks and side hair...

Now I'm planning a thin gold circlet ring to wrap around the forehead, positioned at an elliptical radius so it follows the skull's curve, likely built as a closed loop surface sweep.

Still tuning circlet dimensions...

For the gem accent, I'll add a small teal glowing pendant centered at the front of the circlet, attached to the head bone like the hair. Then I'm moving on to the torso clothing: a green cel-shaded tunic with gold trim along the collar and hem, a belt with a pouch at the waist, and a baldric strap crossing from shoulder to hip to hold a quiver on the back.

Drawing the drape path across the chest and back for the baldric...

Now I'm placing the quiver as a tilted cylinder on the back near the right shoulder, running from a low base point up past the shoulder, giving it tapered radii and a leather material tied to the chest bone, with a gold rim ring at top and five arrow shafts poking out above with fletching.

I'm adding the arrows now—thin rods for shafts extending up from inside the quiver, with a thicker colored band near the top to suggest fletching feathers and nocks, varying the fletching colors across the five arrows and fanning their top positions slightly, plus gold decorative bands at intervals along the quiver body.

I'm also adding a dagger with sheath on the right hip and a small pouch with a flap near the hip.

Now I'm designing bracers for both wrists -- leather cylinders with gold ring stripes and lacing rods, sized to taper with the arm from shoulder to wrist.

I'm also building the shoulder sleeves and pauldrons using half-dome spheres scaled and tilted outward at each shoulder joint, positioned to flare naturally over the puffed sleeve geometry.

Adding the gold rim torus...

Dome scale should give a slightly elliptical cap shape, which should look roughly right even without perfect axis alignment. I also need to add the sleeve spheres at the shoulders, a decorative gold leaf brooch with a glowing gem on the chest, and a flared skirt hem swept around the hips using a lathe shape.

Still refining skirt geometry...

I realize the tabard would be hidden inside the skirt's radius at that height, so I need to reposition the tabard panel to sit flush on the skirt's outer surface instead.

Since a flat tabard can't follow the skirt's curved silhouette, I'm dropping it entirely and instead decorating the skirt directly with paint -- adding a front-center panel using a conditional on position to create a gold chevron stripe. Now I'm sketching the cape as an extruded outline starting from the shoulders.

Still writing cape outline...

I'm trying to tilt the cape backward by adjusting the extrusion direction vector, checking different tilt values to see where the hem lands relative to the skirt radius at various heights, aiming to keep the cape clear of the skirt geometry without overshooting.

Now I'm checking the thickness vector orientation and verifying the cape doesn't collide with the shoulder/arm geometry as it extends down, and thinking through where the quiver sits relative to the cape in front/back positioning.

I need the quiver's center z-position to stay beyond the cape's back plane so it stays visible from behind, adjusting base and top coordinates so the radius clears the cape surface at each height. I'm also offsetting the quiver sideways toward the right shoulder with a slight lean, held by a strap, and now moving on to figuring out the cape's coloring.

For the cape I'm thinking green with a painted grain pattern using cel-shading with subtle streaks along the y-axis to suggest folds, plus a gold trim along the hem -- trying to figure out how to mark the trim using surface position or normal direction rather than a strict pattern.

Writing cloak paint function...

I'm also planning to add a bunched-up hood shape behind the neck using a flattened, scaled sphere to suggest gathered fabric.

For the lower body I'm sketching legs with swept geometry for hips and thighs, dark leggings, and tall brown boots using a leather-grain paint with gold cuffs and tiny box-geometry rods for the front laces.

Still working out boot lacing...

Defining the leg radius curve piecewise...

I'm checking that the skin smoothly follows the hip-knee-ankle chain, then adding foot parts like the toe capsule and boot sole, plus verifying the limb function's bend parameter can take a single direction shared across joints.

Now I'm walking through the actual leg measurements -- hip to ankle distance, the small forward knee bend angle, and foot capsule placement -- to make sure the proportions produce a natural standing pose without the geometry clipping into itself.

I'm adding a heel block and a sole slab to keep the foot grounded properly, checking the floor contact points and widths between hip and foot joints so the legs and feet line up without gaps or overlap. Now I'm shifting to planning the arm chain's structure.

For arms I'm tapering the radius from shoulder to elbow to wrist, splitting the sleeve into bands so the upper arm stays covered while the forearm is bare with a gold trim cuff ring marking the sleeve's end. For the hands, I'm sketching relaxed fingers as small curved capsule segments plus a thumb on the right hand.

Working out finger placement...

Now I'm computing the left hand position on the bow grip, deriving the fist center from the forearm direction and extending the hand along that vector.

I check whether the palm capsule collides with the grip rod, adjusting coordinates slightly so the palm sits snugly against the grip rather than overlapping it, then simplify by aligning the wrist x-position with the bow's grip x-position.

I'm defining the finger capsules as curved paths wrapping around the front of the grip, computing enough points at varying y-values so each finger arcs over the grip's radius and tucks in behind it.

I'm sizing the grip leather rod to run the length of the handle and checking that the palm capsule's z-extent nests just behind the grip's surface so the fist reads as wrapped around it rather than floating in front.

Now I'm wiring the bow to ride the left wrist joint through the arm chain, and settling on eye, hair, and skin colors for a cel-shaded elven look—teal-green iris, pale cream hair with a subtle grain shader, warm skin tone.

Working out the braid's path down the back relative to the cape's curve so the hair chain tucks naturally against the cape geometry without clipping, keeping the palette limited mostly to flat cel paints with threshold-based shading.

Checking the shoulder sphere geometry, the braid keeps colliding with the torso and mantle ring at these coordinates, so I'm nudging the path inward and adjusting the z-depth near the neck to avoid clipping through the chest surface.

Instead I'll route the braid down the back along the cape, offsetting its x position to the left side and tracking the cape's receding z-depth as it falls from the shoulders to the waist, keeping the braid just outside the cape surface at each height.

I'm repositioning the quiver to lean toward the right side, angling its base and top coordinates away from the braid to avoid overlapping geometry, checking that their radii leave enough clearance given the skirt's back depth too.

For the braid, I'm setting up a chevron-style color pattern using a striping function based on position, tapering the radius from thicker at the top to thinner near the tip, then defining the joint chain with named segments for each span of the braid.

I'm also adding a second mass of loose hair sweeping down the back of the head toward the shoulders, built from several tapered strands splayed outward, and checking their depth against the cape so the strands sit just in front without clipping through it.

Adding a small feather charm near the braid, then moving on to other accessories: a dagger and pouch at the belt, boot details, and keeping gloves off while giving only the bow arm a leather bracer for asymmetry. I'm working out the belt loop by sweeping a path around the torso at the chest circumference, finding the smallest fitting loop around that point.

Still writing belt geometry...

Adding a leather pouch box with flap and button on the right hip, then positioning a dagger sheath on the left hip, checking its radius against the skirt's outer taper so it sits just outside the fabric.

For the gems I'm planning to use small glowing spheres with flat emissive colors, maybe adding a few along the bow grip for extra shine. The head stays neutral and the right hand stays empty and relaxed rather than holding an arrow.

Now I need to write the final code carefully, making sure I only import what's actually used (THREE and the builder helper) to avoid unused-import errors.

Setting up the cel-shaded color palette...

Finalizing wood and string colors, plus glow and ink accents, then setting up the gold-rimmed leather pauldron before starting the build script with the archer rig imports and builder setup.

Building hip and spine joints...

Adding sleeve spheres positioned relative to torso half-width, then defining the lower torso stations for hips, waist, and chest with their widths and heights going up the loft.

I'm checking the taper near the shoulder top and neck transition—the rounding cap radius ends up larger than intended, creating a bulb-like bump around the base of the neck that reads like a trapezius muscle rather than a clean taper, so I need to adjust the shoulder slope stations to avoid that artifact.

Now I'm defining the loft stations for the torso (switching the end cap to flat instead of round so it doesn't bulge), then moving on to the tunic's painted details—adding a gold center front trim line and considering a V-neckline pattern.

Still building the head geometry... adding a neck sweep for the chain, then shaping the skull and jaw spheres with skin coloring attached to their bones.

Now I'm setting up eye decals to project onto the skull surface, placing them after the hair bangs so timing doesn't conflict. Then I'm extruding ear shapes symmetrically on both sides using mirrored x-offsets and tapered thickness profiles.

Working out the ear tip orientation for both sides, then adding a small gold earring ring near the lobe, positioning and rotating it to hang naturally.

For the hair, I'm building a partial sphere cap scaled and tilted to fit the skull, then layering a smaller volume on top for extra crown fullness, and starting to arrange a row of bangs along the front hairline.

Now I'm sweeping curved spike shapes for individual bangs, tapering each from a flat base to a pointed tip, and checking that their positions sit just above the hairline so the tips clear the skull surface near the forehead.

For the side locks, I'm sweeping tapered curves running from near the temple down past the ear toward the collar, making sure they overlap the ear region slightly in front without clipping into the skull geometry.

Still writing hair strands...

Now adding the circlet with gem and feather earring, then sweeping the braid as a chain with small gold ties at intervals and a spike-shaped tassel at the tip.

For the arms, I'm defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions symmetrically for both sides, naming them with L/R suffixes and treating left as +X, right as -X in world space.

I'm then setting up a tapering radius function for the arm that narrows from shoulder to wrist, with a sweep that applies sleeve material up to 60% of the arm length and skin material beyond that, including a gold trim band at the sleeve edge.

I'm exposing the arm's joint positions (shoulder, elbow, wrist) for attaching accessories, then adding a shoulder pad sphere riding the shoulder joint and a leather bracer cylinder oriented along the forearm's tangent frame, which I'll cap with gold rings.

Still adding bracer details...

Now I'm positioning the right hand relaxed with wrist, direction vector, and palm placement computed, then laying out knuckle positions for each finger spaced along the front-back axis.

Writing finger joint math...

Working out the boot geometry next—adding a curled elven toe spike and a sole box positioned to meet the ankle capsule and toe tip cleanly.

Now I'm defining the toe joint parented to the ankle, debating whether to tag it with a "digit" role, and deciding to leave it unlabeled for simplicity before moving on to assembling the rest of the rig code.

I'm computing a mantle ring around the neck base, using an elliptical curve that dips slightly in front to match the shoulder slope, then building a closed catmull tube with the cloak color and chest bone attachment, checking that its radius covers the torso's flat top ledge.

Adding a second smaller standing collar ring higher up, sizing it so its inner edge still overlaps the neck radius, then planning a small leaf-shaped brooch clasp at the front where the mantle ends meet.

Writing brooch and skirt lathe geometry...

Checking whether the thigh radius at hip height pokes outside the skirt profile, since the thigh's outer reach at x .17 might exceed the skirt's radius there, so I need to verify clearance between legs and skirt hem.

Zigzag hem profile looks fine, and I'll add a separate hanging front panel like a loincloth strip slightly outside the skirt, computing its radius growth with depth so it drapes naturally over the skirt surface.

Adjusting the slope to [0,1,-0.3] brings the depth calculations closer to matching the skirt outline at each cross-section, and the resulting cross product confirms the correct front-facing thickness vector.

Now I'm shaping the tabard outline with a sharp bottom point and tapered sides, and thinking through how to paint it in cream and gold with a chevron embroidery pattern using surface coordinates to mask the border bands and lines.

Still defining tabard colors and gold chevron pattern...

Still writing quiver paint logic...

For the arrows, I'll generate 6 small offset vectors to fan them out from the quiver's top opening, with each arrow running from a point near the base up through the top plus its offset, slightly flared for a natural bundled look.

Now I'm setting up the fletching: a helper function that takes a start point, tip, and feather color, computes the unit direction toward the tip, and places two fletching bands near the tip using vector math for positioning.

For bones, I'm thinking arrow rod arrays won't have proper bone attachments, so I'll bind them to the nearest joint and set the chest bone as the anchor, making sure the arrows stay tucked inside the quiver without poking through the cape.

For the strap, I'm draping a path along the torso surface using a closed catmull-rom curve, sweeping a thin leather tube along it with lift applied so it hugs the back and chest contours realistically.

Now I'm working out the strap route crossing from the left hip over the right shoulder toward the quiver on the back, adding a row of gold studs placed along the draped path at even intervals, then setting up the belt loop around the waist and a dagger sheath rod on the left hip with a tapered radius and a gold tip sphere at the end.

Next I'm adding the dagger hilt itself: a grip rod, a small gold guard box, and a gold pommel sphere positioned above the sheath. Then I'm layering in facial finishing touches like lashes and mouth detail within the decal, plus small extras like tunic seam lines and sleeves, and considering a teal feather charm accessory near the braid.

Writing feather geometry...

I should bind these accessories to the head bone, and double check the gem glow uses a flat color from the part data. For the bow, I'm adding gold band details and considering a small gem accent near the grip.

Now I'm working out the bowstring geometry — a thin rod connecting the tips — and rigging the bow to the wrist joint. I'm adding spike nocks at the bow tips and confirming the bow's position clears the leg and stays above the floor.

For the head, I'm checking proportions: overall height, hair crown height, and eye placement relative to head center, then placing eye decals with calculated position and size to sit correctly on the skull's curved surface.

Now I'm finalizing the piece list and checking for unused variables before writing the full code.

Writing the leg loop, generating limb points from hip to foot target for each side symmetrically.

Still designing the boot cuff geometry...

Now I'm working out the laces, sweeping small diagonal rods along the leg at alternating angles to simulate crisscross lacing, with thin pale-colored cylinders for each stitch.

Moving on to the foot parts and weighted bones, binding pieces to the ankle joint from the leg chain, then shifting attention to the cape and hood geometry.

I'm writing a helper function that builds an arrow shape: computing the direction vector between two points, drawing a wooden shaft rod, then adding feather rods offset along that direction near the tip.

Still writing arrow code...

I'm figuring out the nock and fletching details—keeping the fletch as tapered rods rather than flat vanes for simplicity, and confirming the paint type usage lines up with the cel instances already created before the builder runs. Now I'm moving on to the hair and top details before finalizing the piece.

Writing sleeve and hair geometry...

I'm setting up the tunic paint function, defining color regions based on surface normal and vertical position to separate the front panel from the rest of the garment.

Writing cape paint logic...

I realize using a fixed shadow color breaks shading on gold trim since it would force dark green shadows everywhere—better to use cel with just the lit paint and let the shadow derive per-color automatically. I'll apply this same unshaded approach to the tabard and hair grain, then move on to defining the skirt paint...

Writing paint logic...

I should also double-check for unused variables like armSweep and legSweep, making sure each declared helper actually gets used somewhere in the final output before writing the file.
